literal: The old frontiersman lost his horse
meaning: A blessing in disguise / Misfortune may turn into fortune
story: Huainanzi: when an old man lost a horse, it returned with a fine steed; when his son broke his leg riding it, he was spared the draft.

literal: Drawing a snake and adding feet
meaning: To spoil something by adding superfluous details / Overdoing it
story: Zhan Guo Ce: contestants raced to draw a snake; the first finished early and arrogantly added feet, losing the prize.

literal: A frog at the bottom of a well
meaning: A person with a narrow worldview and limited horizons
story: Zhuangzi: a frog in a well boasted of his world until a sea turtle described the vastness of the boundless ocean.

literal: Guarding a tree stump waiting for rabbits
meaning: Relying on a one-time fluke instead of putting in real work
story: Han Feizi: a hare ran into a stump and died; the lazy farmer quit plowing and waited forever for more hares.

literal: Plugging one's ears to steal a bell
meaning: Deceiving oneself / Refusing to face the obvious truth
story: Lüshi Chunqiu: a thief stole a heavy bell and plugged his own ears to muffle the sound, foolishly thinking no one could hear it.

literal: Carving a notch on the boat to find the lost sword
meaning: Using rigid, outdated methods in a changed situation
story: Lüshi Chunqiu: a man dropped his sword into a river and notched his boat's side to dive for it when the boat docked.

literal: Mending the pen after sheep are lost
meaning: Better late than never / Taking action after a setback to prevent further damage
story: Zhan Guo Ce: after a wolf took some sheep, the shepherd promptly repaired the hole in the fence to protect the flock.

literal: Pulling up young shoots to help them grow
meaning: Spoiling things by counterproductive haste / Forcing unnatural growth
story: Mencius: an impatient farmer yanked his rice shoots upward to make them grow faster; they all withered by evening.

literal: The fox borrowing the tiger's majesty
meaning: Bullying others by flaunting someone else's authority
story: Zhan Guo Ce: a clever fox walked ahead of a tiger to pretend all forest animals fled in fear of him.

literal: The lance and shield clashing with each other
meaning: Self-contradictory / An inconsistent or illogical claim
story: Han Feizi: a vendor boasted his spear could pierce any shield, and his shield could block any spear.

literal: The bow's reflection mistaken for a snake in the wine cup
meaning: Paranoia and unnecessary fear caused by false suspicions
story: A guest fell sick believing he swallowed a snake; his host demonstrated it was only the reflection of a painted bow.

literal: Pretending to play the reed pipe to make up numbers
meaning: Passing oneself off as qualified / Padding the numbers with fakes
story: King Xuan of Qi liked 300-man pipe orchestras; Mr. Nanguo pretended to play until the new king demanded solo recitals.

literal: Three in the morning, four in the evening
meaning: Capricious and fickle / Tricking someone with superficial changes
story: Zhuangzi: a monkey trainer offered 3 nuts at morning and 4 at night; when monkeys were angry, he switched to 4 morning and 3 night.

literal: Quenching thirst by imagining sour plums
meaning: Consoling oneself with illusions / Encouraging people through hope
story: Cao Cao marched his parched troops across a dry plain by shouting that a grove of tart plums lay ahead, making their mouths water.

literal: Pointing at a deer and calling it a horse
meaning: Deliberately reversing right and wrong / Bullying people into submission through lies
story: Shiji: eunuch Zhao Gao presented a stag to court, daring officials to disagree and executing those who told the truth.

literal: Playing the zither to a grazing ox
meaning: Addressing an unappreciative audience / Explaining deep ideas to someone who cannot grasp them
story: Master Gongming Yi played sublime ancient melodies to an ox, which completely ignored him and went on eating grass.

literal: The man of Qi worrying that the sky will fall
meaning: Groundless anxiety / Baseless worry about imaginary disasters
story: Liezi: a man in the state of Qi lost sleep and appetite fearing the vault of heaven would crack and collapse on him.

literal: Lord Ye's professed passion for dragons
meaning: Pretending to love something in theory but dreading the reality
story: Lord Ye carved dragons on all his walls; when a real celestial dragon flew down to visit, he fled in terror.

literal: Blind men touching an elephant
meaning: Mistaking a partial glimpse for the whole truth / Biased perspective
story: Buddhist canon: several blind men touched different parts of an elephant and quarreled over whether it was a rope, snake, or wall.

literal: Buying the ornamental case and returning the pearl
meaning: Showing poor judgment by valuing packaging over substance
story: Han Feizi: a craftsman decorated a box with gold and perfume; a customer bought it and returned the precious pearl inside.

literal: Shafts pointing south while heading for the north
meaning: Acting contrary to one's goal / Defeating one's own purpose
story: Zhan Guo Ce: a traveler wanted to reach the southern state of Chu, but steered his carriage toward the frozen north.

literal: The foolish old man moving mountains
meaning: Unyielding perseverance overcoming seemingly insurmountable odds
story: Liezi: an elderly man vowed his descendants would chisel away two giant peaks blocking their village until the heavens took pity.

literal: Jingwei bird filling the boundless sea
meaning: Tenacious, tireless spirit fighting against impossible odds
story: Shan Hai Jing: the drowned daughter of the Flame Emperor became a bird, carrying twigs and stones day after day to fill the ocean.

literal: Kuafu chasing after the blazing sun
meaning: Unyielding ambition to pursue an impossible ideal
story: Shan Hai Jing: giant Kuafu raced the sun across deserts, dying of thirst and turning his wooden staff into an orchard.

literal: When the lips are gone, the teeth feel the cold
meaning: Interdependent survival; if one ally falls, the other is doomed
story: Zuo Zhuan: when Guo fell to Jin, neighboring Yu lost its buffer and was promptly swallowed as well.

literal: Returning the jade intact to the state of Zhao
meaning: Returning a precious item safely to its rightful owner against all odds
story: Lin Xiangru took the sacred Heshi Jade to treacherous Qin and returned it without a scratch through sheer courage and wit.

literal: Mao Sui volunteering his own talents
meaning: Stepping forward boldly to volunteer one's abilities / Self-nomination
story: Mao Sui stepped out from a crowd of retainers to represent Zhao in diplomatic talks with Chu, sealing a crucial pact.

literal: Having the complete bamboo in one's mind before painting
meaning: Having a well-thought-out plan in advance / Confident and prepared
story: Song painter Wen Tong observed bamboo through all seasons so that every stroke was clear in his mind before touching paper.

literal: The donkey of Qian has exhausted its meager tricks
meaning: Having run out of ideas / At one's wits' end
story: Liu Zongyuan: a tiger in Guizhou was initially afraid of a newly introduced donkey until it realized the donkey could only kick.

literal: Swinging an axe in front of master carpenter Lu Ban
meaning: Showing off amateur skill before an undisputed master
story: Displaying elementary craft before legendary carpenter Lu Ban; showing false modesty or foolish bravado.

literal: Carrying thorny birch rods on one's back to ask for pardon
meaning: Humbly and sincerely apologizing for past misconduct
story: General Lian Po of Zhao, humbled by minister Lin Xiangru's magnanimity, stripped bare and carried brambles to Lin's door.

literal: An old horse knows the way back
meaning: An experienced veteran knows the ropes / Value of past experience
story: Han Feizi: Guan Zhong and Duke Huan lost their path in a blizzard; releasing an old horse led the entire army home safely.

literal: Discussing military warfare on paper
meaning: Theoretical chatter detached from real-world practice / Armchair general
story: Zhao Kuo could quote Sun Tzu flawlessly but had zero field experience; appointed general, his army was wiped out at Changping.

literal: The sound of wind and the cry of cranes
meaning: Extreme panic where every trivial sound sparks terror
story: At the Battle of Fei River, routed soldiers fled in darkness mistaking the whistling wind and screaming birds for pursuing cavalry.

literal: Every bush and tree looks like an enemy soldier
meaning: Severe paranoia where every harmless shadow appears threatening
story: Defeated emperor Fu Jian looked up at Bagong Mountain and hallucinated that bushes were enemy soldiers waiting in ambush.

literal: With the irresistible force of splitting bamboo
meaning: Irresistible momentum sweeping past every obstacle
story: Once a sharp knife splits the first two joints of bamboo, the remaining stalk splits open cleanly without effort.

literal: When the waters recede, the hidden rocks emerge
meaning: The truth finally comes to light / Concealed facts become evident
story: Su Shi: as autumn winds drain the mountain creeks, every boulder lying below the surface is exposed.

literal: Repairing the nest before the storm begins
meaning: Taking precautions before crisis hits / Preparing for a rainy day
story: Book of Songs: birds gather twigs and thatch to reinforce their nests before the summer rain pours.

literal: Preventing troubles before they ignite
meaning: Nipping dangers in the bud / Preventive prudence
story: Taking decisive security steps early so disasters are extinguished before they can ever take root.

literal: Grasping the large outcome from a microscopic sign
meaning: Inferring significant trends from tiny early indications
story: Han Feizi: a truly wise ruler spots historical turning points from the most minute initial signs.

literal: Reflecting on peril while living in peace
meaning: Staying vigilant during good times / Never growing complacent
story: Zuo Zhuan: one who prepares for adversity during times of tranquility will never suffer sudden ruin.

literal: Smashing cooking cauldrons and sinking the crossing boats
meaning: Cutting off all retreat / Full commitment with no fallback option
story: Xiang Yu crossed the Zhang River, sank all transports and smashed cauldrons to leave his troops no choice but total victory.

literal: Sleeping on firewood and tasting bitter gall
meaning: Enduring severe hardship to steel one's resolve and triumph
story: King Goujian of Yue slept on thorny brushwood and tasted gall daily for 20 years to never forget his defeat until he conquered Wu.

literal: Tying hair to the rafter and jabbing the thigh with an awl
meaning: Studying with extraordinary diligence and self-discipline
story: Sun Jing tied his hair to a roof beam; Su Qin poked his thigh with an awl whenever sleep overcame him during midnight study.

literal: Rising to practice swordplay at the first rooster crow
meaning: Self-disciplined preparation and early rising for great ambition
story: Generals Zu Ti and Liu Kun rose at the first midnight crow to practice swordplay under the stars to serve their nation.

literal: Proficiency comes from continuous practice
meaning: Practice makes perfect
story: Chen Yaoci was a haughty archer; an old oil seller proved true mastery by pouring oil through a coin hole without a drop spilled.

literal: Lifting one corner and inferring the other three
meaning: Learning through analogy / Inferring broad principles from a single example
story: Confucius: if a teacher explains one corner of a square and the student cannot infer the remaining three, the lesson stops.

literal: Reviewing old knowledge to discover new insights
meaning: Gaining fresh understanding by reviewing past experience
story: Confucius: one who constantly reflects on acquired wisdom and uncovers new angles is worthy of teaching others.

literal: Following proper order and advancing step by step
meaning: Making steady, methodical progress
story: Zhu Xi: true learning requires systematic progress, solidifying each step before attempting the next.

literal: Working tirelessly without fatigue
meaning: Diligently persevering with unflagging dedication
story: Shiji: immersing oneself completely in books and research without ever showing weariness.

literal: Silently influencing and imperceptibly transforming
meaning: Subtle, unconscious transformation over time
story: A person's mindset and values are shaped gradually and quietly by the culture and role models surrounding them.

literal: Half the effort yielding double the result
meaning: Achieving high efficiency through smart methods
story: Mencius: applying proper timing and principles achieves immense gains with half the customary labor.

literal: Laboring in vain with zero reward
meaning: Wasted effort / Futile striving
story: Exerting immense labor and resources without yielding any practical result.

literal: Constant water drops wear through rock
meaning: Relentless perseverance conquers the hardest obstacles
story: Trivial droplets falling steadily over years will pierce granite; continuous small steps achieve monumental goals.

literal: A rope saws through wood over time
meaning: Persistent gradual effort achieves astonishing feats
story: Just as water pierces rock, consistent friction from soft hemp rope eventually cuts through thick wood.

literal: Chiseling without stopping
meaning: Relentless dedication / Never giving up
story: Xunzi: if you stop carving, dry wood won't break; if you carve without stopping, gold and stone can be engraved.

literal: Giving up halfway along the path
meaning: Abandoning an endeavor before it is finished
story: Liji: quitting midway through a journey forfeits all previous progress.

literal: Falling short by a single basket of earth
meaning: Failing at the very brink of success for want of one last push
story: Shangshu: building a nine-fathom mound and stopping just one basketful short ruins the entire effort.

literal: All previous achievements thrown away
meaning: All past hard work going to waste
story: A single blunder or sudden surrender destroying all the fruits of past labor.

literal: Beating the grass and startling the snake
meaning: Inadvertently alerting an opponent through hasty moves
story: From 36 Stratagems: reckless early agitation warns the lurking foe, giving them time to prepare or flee.

literal: Luring the tiger away from its mountain stronghold
meaning: Enticing an adversary away from their stronghold
story: From 36 Stratagems: drawing a formidable opponent out into unfamiliar, vulnerable terrain.

literal: Borrowing another's blade to strike
meaning: Using a third party to do one's dirty work
story: From 36 Stratagems: eliminating an adversary through someone else's hands without dirtying one's own.

literal: Besieging Wei to rescue Zhao
meaning: Relieving pressure on an ally by attacking the enemy's vulnerable rear
story: When Wei attacked Handan, Sun Bin attacked Wei's capital Daliang, forcing the Wei army to withdraw immediately.

literal: The golden cicada shedding its shell
meaning: Slipping away unnoticed while leaving behind an empty illusion
story: From 36 Stratagems: escaping danger by leaving behind a decoy while the real body vanishes.

literal: Clamoring in the east while striking in the west
meaning: Feigning an attack in one spot while striking another
story: From 36 Stratagems: making a noisy diversion on one flank while the real assault hits elsewhere.

literal: Secretly crossing at Chencang
meaning: Making a surprise move while keeping the public distracted
story: Han Xin openly repaired wooden trestle bridges to deceive the enemy while secretly marching through Chencang.

literal: Watching the fire burn from across the river
meaning: Detachedly watching others suffer or fight among themselves
story: From 36 Stratagems: standing by until rivals exhaust each other before stepping in.

literal: Hiding a dagger behind a warm smile
meaning: Treacherous malice disguised as friendly warmth
story: From 36 Stratagems: greeting someone with radiant affection while plotting their destruction.

literal: The plum tree dying in place of the peach
meaning: One party sacrificing or taking the blame for another
story: Sacrificing a minor asset or taking a temporary hit to preserve the core interest.

literal: Leading away a sheep with a passing hand
meaning: Seizing a convenient, opportunistic opening / Taking advantage of a loophole
story: From 36 Stratagems: taking advantage of a minor oversight to gain an easy benefit.

literal: Pulling the burning firewood from under the pot
meaning: Tackling a problem at its root rather than treating symptoms
story: To stop boiling broth from spilling over, extinguish the firewood beneath the pot.

literal: Catching fish in muddy waters
meaning: Taking advantage of chaos and confusion for selfish gain
story: Muddying the river to disorient the fish so they can be easily snatched.

literal: Letting go in order to capture more securely
meaning: Playing the long game by giving an opponent slack before tightening the net
story: Zhuge Liang captured and freed rebel Meng Huo seven times until his heart was genuinely won over.

literal: Throwing out a brick to attract a jade gem
meaning: Offering a modest initial remark to elicit brilliant insights from others
story: A modest opening formula in Chinese speeches and scholarly discussions.

literal: The empty fortress strategy
meaning: A daring bluff against overwhelming forces when totally defenseless
story: Zhuge Liang threw open the gates of Xicheng and played his zither peacefully, blunting Sima Yi's army.

literal: The ruse of inflicting pain on oneself
meaning: Staging self-harm to gain the enemy's trust
story: Huang Gai endured brutal public flogging to make Cao Cao believe in his fake defection at Red Cliff.

literal: The counter-espionage strategy
meaning: Using the enemy's spies to sow internal mistrust in their own ranks
story: From 36 Stratagems: turning an opponent's intelligence agents into unwitting conduits of disinformation.

literal: Retreating is the best course of action
meaning: Tactical withdrawal when facing impossible odds
story: From 36 Stratagems: when all other moves fail, retreating to fight another day is supreme wisdom.

literal: Holding on without slacking
meaning: Persevering unremittingly / Never giving up
story: Persisting day after day through hardships without losing momentum.

literal: Unbending despite a hundred fractures
meaning: Indomitable spirit / Unyielding after countless setbacks
story: Standing tall with courage no matter how many times one is defeated.

literal: Striving constantly for self-improvement
meaning: Ceaseless self-strengthening and personal growth
story: From Yijing: Heaven moves with cosmic vigor; the noble person strives tirelessly to improve.

literal: Undeterred by wind or rain
meaning: Regardless of weather or difficulties / Rain or shine
story: Carrying out a mission or appointment no matter what obstacle arises.

literal: Committing one's entire strength to the goal
meaning: Going all out / Putting in 100% effort
story: Devoting all physical and mental energy to accomplish an important task.

literal: Advancing directly into difficulties
meaning: Facing obstacles head-on / Rising to the challenge
story: Courageously tackling the hardest part of a problem first.

literal: Marching courageously straight forward
meaning: Forging boldly ahead without fear
story: Advancing without hesitation through danger and adversity.

literal: Striving to swim upstream
meaning: Striving for the best / Aiming high
story: Constantly pushing oneself to excel and reach the top tier.

literal: Determined to make oneself strong
meaning: Working hard to forge prosperity and strength
story: Channeling frustration into fuel for self-empowerment and national renewal.

literal: Seeking tirelessly day and night
meaning: Diligently and earnestly pursuing a goal
story: Pursuing mastery or knowledge without pausing for distraction.

literal: Consistent from beginning to end
meaning: Remaining unchanged and faithful throughout
story: Maintaining the very same devotion from the first day to the last.

literal: Forgetting sleep and neglecting meals
meaning: Utterly absorbed in work or study
story: So passionately engaged that one loses track of food and bedtime.

literal: Connecting night to day
meaning: Working around the clock without rest
story: Carrying on labor straight through the night into the following morning.

literal: Cautious, attentive, and dedicated
meaning: Diligent and conscientious in one's duties
story: Working with careful vigilance and absolute responsibility.

literal: Feet planted firmly on solid ground
meaning: Pragmatic, down-to-earth, and thorough
story: Doing real work step by step instead of chasing airy fantasies.

literal: Bearing bitterness and enduring toil
meaning: Hardworking and capable of enduring hardship
story: Working steadfastly under rough, demanding conditions.

literal: Sharpening beaks and fighting again
meaning: Making sustained efforts / Continuing to push forward
story: Originating from cockfighting; keeping up momentum after a preliminary triumph.

literal: Grinding an iron pestle into an embroidery needle
meaning: With endless perseverance, even a huge metal bar can be ground into a needle
story: Li Bai saw an old woman grinding an iron rod by a stream; inspired, he rededicated himself to study.

literal: The clumsy bird flies early
meaning: The less gifted must start earlier and work harder
story: A modest expression for compensating lack of innate talent with early preparation.

literal: Heaven rewards the diligent
meaning: Hard work pays off / God helps those who work hard
story: From the Book of Changes: nature favors those who invest sincere effort and persistence.

literal: Water-grinding patience
meaning: Patient, meticulous craft that takes endless time
story: Producing extraordinary results through subtle, patient, incremental effort.

literal: Experiencing every bitter hardship
meaning: Weathering countless tribulations and trials
story: Overcoming countless ordeals before reaching the final triumph.

literal: Firm and persistent, incapable of being dislodged
meaning: Unyielding grit and tenacity
story: Enduring severe suffering without budging an inch from one's ideals.

literal: Ceasing only upon death
meaning: Bowing down to exert all effort until one's dying breath
story: Zhuge Liang pledged to labor for Shu Han until the end of his days.

literal: Firm and unswerving
meaning: Steadfast, unwavering, and rock solid
story: Holding to a principle without being deflected by outside pressure.

literal: Advancing relentlessly with nothing in front to stop it
meaning: Charging forward undaunted / Unstoppable drive
story: Marching onward with heroic determination, crushing all barriers.

literal: Facing danger without fear
meaning: Undismayed in the face of mortal danger
story: Maintaining composure and courage when sudden catastrophe strikes.

literal: Possessing great wisdom and immense courage
meaning: Combining supreme intellect with fearless bravery
story: A leader endowed with both profound strategic vision and physical valor.

literal: Throwing oneself forward without regard for personal safety
meaning: Selfless courage in charging forward
story: Leaping into danger to save comrades or complete a vital mission.

literal: Rather die than surrender
meaning: Choosing death over dishonor / Unbending integrity
story: Refusing to yield to enemy coercion even on pain of execution.

literal: Standing high and gazing far
meaning: Farsighted / Possessing visionary strategic perspective
story: Looking past short-term noise to perceive long-term historic trends.

literal: Deep planning and far-reaching forethought
meaning: Calculating shrewdly for long-term contingencies
story: Formulating strategies that anticipate developments years ahead.

literal: Knowing yourself and knowing your adversary
meaning: Know yourself and know your enemy, and you will never lose
story: From Sun Tzu: complete awareness of both sides guarantees victory in a hundred battles.

literal: Devising plans and laying out strategies
meaning: Giving advice / Formulating strategic proposals
story: Acting as a trusted strategist who devises effective solutions.

literal: Divine foresight and marvelous calculations
meaning: Brilliant foresight and masterly strategy
story: Praising strategists like Zhuge Liang whose military predictions seemed magical.

literal: Appraising the times and weighing the situation
meaning: Judging the opportune moment and adapting to changing conditions
story: Carefully reading current circumstances before making a major move.

literal: Adapting to whatever situation arises
meaning: Acting flexibly according to circumstances / Thinking on one's feet
story: Not clinging rigidly to doctrine, but pivoting as conditions evolve.

literal: Winning a hundred battles out of a hundred
meaning: Victorious in every single encounter / Invincible
story: Consistently outmaneuvering rivals across every campaign.

literal: War never tires of deception
meaning: All warfare is based on deception / Deceit is fair in war
story: From Han Feizi: battlefield strategy inherently relies on misleading the enemy.

literal: Gathering diverse thoughts to broaden benefit
meaning: Pooling collective wisdom to reach the best decision
story: Zhuge Liang encouraged subordinates to debate freely so all insights could be leveraged.

literal: Listening to both sides yields clarity
meaning: Listening to diverse viewpoints avoids bias
story: From Wei Zheng to Tang Emperor Taizong: listening to all sides enlightens; believing one blinds.

literal: Listening to only one side brings darkness
meaning: Biased listening leads to delusion
story: Complement of 兼听则明: trusting only one faction leaves a ruler in the dark.

literal: Moving calculation rods inside the command tent
meaning: Devising master strategies behind the scenes
story: Han Gaozu praised Zhang Liang for planning victories from inside his headquarters tent.

literal: Deciding victory a thousand miles away
meaning: Securing decisive victory across distant frontiers through grand strategy
story: Complement of 运筹帷幄: commanding theater-wide victory from afar.

literal: Fortifying a camp with every single step
meaning: Advancing cautiously and methodically consolidating every gain
story: Making sure every step forward is fortified so retreat is never necessary.

literal: Using softness to overcome hardness
meaning: Yielding to conquer / Overcoming brute force with flexibility
story: From Laozi: soft water wears away rigid rock; flexibility overcomes rigidity.

literal: Supreme craftsmanship looks simple and clumsy
meaning: True genius appears modest and unaffected
story: From Daodejing: ultimate skill does not show off; it seems natural and effortless.

literal: Supreme wisdom appears like foolishness
meaning: A truly wise person maintains humility and rarely shows off
story: From Su Shi: people of profound wisdom don't flaunt their cleverness in trivial matters.

literal: Things reaching extremes must reverse direction
meaning: When things reach the extreme, they swing to the opposite / Extremes meet
story: Classical Daoist philosophy: prosperity at its peak turns to decline; winter yields to spring.

literal: Seeking truth from actual facts
meaning: Pragmatic / Grounded in realistic empirical evidence
story: From Han Shu: investigating genuine facts to derive objective truths.

literal: Steering the rudder according to the wind
meaning: Trimming one's sails / Adaptable or opportunistically shifting stances
story: Can mean smartly adapting to circumstances or opportunistically changing loyalties.

literal: Throwing a stone to test the path ahead
meaning: Probing the situation cautiously before making a major move
story: Testing the waters to see how people respond before committing resources.

literal: Hiding one's brightness and biding one's time in obscurity
meaning: Keeping a low profile and building capability quietly
story: Deng Xiaoping's famous foreign policy principle: biding time and concealing strength.

literal: Avoiding enemy strength and striking at emptiness
meaning: Striking where the adversary is weak and avoiding where they are strong
story: From Sun Tzu: an army should be like water, flowing past high ground and surging into voids.

literal: Predicting events like a god
meaning: Extraordinary prophetic foresight
story: Anticipating every twist of events with supernatural accuracy.

literal: Adapting measures to local conditions
meaning: Tailoring solutions to local realities
story: Implementing policies that match specific geographic and cultural circumstances.

literal: Guiding actions according to prevailing trends
meaning: Guiding developments smoothly along existing momentum
story: Using natural momentum to achieve goals with minimal friction.

literal: A step of one's foot tips the balance
meaning: Holding the balance of power / Playing a pivotal, decisive role
story: A key figure whose every decision has huge repercussions for the whole field.

literal: Momentum that cannot be stopped
meaning: Unstoppable / Irresistible force
story: Surging forward with power so vast that nothing can impede it.

literal: Crossing the river in the same boat
meaning: Pulling together through common danger / Solidarity in crisis
story: From Sun Tzu: even ancient enemies in a storm will help each other navigate safely.

literal: The ocean of learning has no shore
meaning: There is no limit to knowledge / Lifelong learning
story: Knowledge is boundless; one must remain humble and keep exploring forever.

literal: Broad, vast, refined, and profound
meaning: Extensive and profound (of culture, philosophy, or learning)
story: Describing grand philosophical traditions or deep cultural heritage.

literal: Learned in antiquity and conversant with the present
meaning: Possessing encyclopedic knowledge of history and contemporary affairs
story: A brilliant scholar who masters classical wisdom while understanding modern realities.

literal: Knowledge filling five carts of bamboo scrolls
meaning: Profoundly learned / Having read widely
story: Zhuangzi praised Hui Shi whose writings and bamboo book scrolls filled five ox-carts.

literal: Possessing eight pecks out of ten of world talent
meaning: Endowed with extraordinary creative genius
story: Xie Lingyun remarked that if global talent were ten measures, Cao Zhi alone held eight.

literal: Rising above the crowd and standing out
meaning: Outstanding / Eminently surpassing one's peers
story: From Mencius: rising above the average flock like an eagle above sparrows.

literal: Standing tall and aloof from the ordinary throng
meaning: Distinguished and exceptional / Far above the mediocre
story: Possessing noble bearing and intellect that distinctly towers above ordinary crowds.

literal: Carved by the axes of ghosts and spirits
meaning: Supernatural craftsmanship / Uncanny artistic mastery
story: Describing breathtaking architecture, intricate carving, or magnificent natural wonders.

literal: Flowers blossoming from a magic brush
meaning: Possessing brilliant literary talent / Gifted writing style
story: Legend says poet Li Bai dreamt his writing brush blossomed with lotus flowers.

literal: Planting a unique banner of one's own
meaning: Carving out a distinct style / Trailblazing
story: Establishing an original school of thought, design, or art distinct from all others.

literal: The furnace fire burns pure blue
meaning: Reaching the pinnacle of technical perfection / Flawless mastery
story: From Daoist alchemy: when the furnace heat burns transparent azure, the elixir is perfected.

literal: Climbing the highest summit and reaching the extreme peak
meaning: Reaching the absolute pinnacle of an art or craft
story: Attaining the very highest level of skill or artistic accomplishment.

literal: Wielding brush and ink with complete freedom
meaning: Expressing oneself with effortless fluidity and grace
story: Painting or writing calligraphy with spontaneous, relaxed confidence.

literal: The butcher's blade glides with room to spare
meaning: Handling a difficult task with effortless ease and mastery
story: Zhuangzi: Cook Ding's cleaver sliced through joints effortlessly because he knew the empty spaces.

literal: Having seen much and known widely
meaning: Experienced and knowledgeable / Well-traveled
story: A worldly person who has experienced diverse regions and cultures.

literal: Deep study yielding personal insight
meaning: Attaining true enlightenment through self-directed study
story: Mencius: deep personal study allows one to internalize wisdom naturally.

literal: Lifting a heavy burden as if it were light
meaning: Handling tremendous challenges with calm composure
story: Managing complex, high-stakes crises with effortless grace.

literal: Painting the dragon and dotting in the eyes
meaning: Adding the vital finishing touch that brings the whole work to life
story: Zhang Sengyou painted dragons without pupils; when he dotted in the eyes, thunder struck and they flew into the clouds.

literal: Every single character is a pearl or gem
meaning: Exquisite writing where every word is priceless
story: Praising essays or poetry of sparkling eloquence and refined vocabulary.

literal: Words flow from the mouth ready to be published
meaning: Eloquent speech that is structured like polished literature
story: Speaking with effortless elegance, eloquence, and literary sophistication.

literal: Pouring out non-stop like a surging torrent
meaning: Talking on and on with unstoppable fluency
story: Speaking with continuous enthusiasm, eloquence, and animation.

literal: Soaked in by the ears and dyed by the eyes
meaning: Subtly influenced by what one constantly hears and sees
story: Absorbing artistic taste or moral character from constant exposure to one's environment.

literal: Methodically and patiently guiding someone forward
meaning: Teaching patiently and skillfully step by step
story: From the Analects: praise for Confucius' gentle, systematic pedagogy that led students to insight.

literal: Opening a book always yields benefit
meaning: Reading is always rewarding / Any book offers knowledge
story: Emperor Taizong of Song read daily, declaring that opening a volume never fails to bring insight.

literal: Not ashamed to ask questions of one's inferiors
meaning: Humble enough to seek knowledge from anyone, regardless of rank
story: From the Analects: true scholars are eager to learn from anyone without false pride.
